card.name: Ori Tahiti
card.tagline: The umbrella of all traditional Tahitian dance.
card.profile: Ori Tahiti ('Tahitian dance') is the umbrella term for the dance traditions of Tahiti and the Society Islands (Bora Bora, Moorea, Raiatea, Tahaa, Huahine). It unites five forms - oteea, aparima, hivinau, paoa and the recitative pataautau - characterized by a divided body (legs mark the percussion rhythm; arms/torso narrate a cultural theme), Tahitian-language song, percussion (toere, pahu) and plant-fiber costumes. Troupes (pupu ori) perform at the Heiva i Tahiti festival - founded in 1881 as 'Tiurai' and renamed Heiva in 1985 - functioning as social cohesion and identity transmission (culture.gouv.fr; Tahiti Tourisme).
card.insight: Banned under the 1819 Pomare Code, the dance was fully revived in 1956 when Madeleine Moua, a Papeete school principal, founded the troupe 'Heiva Tahiti'; the practice was added to France's national intangible-heritage inventory in 2017 (culture.gouv.fr).
card.image_significance: Tahiti's hip-shaking drum dance. A representative image shows grass or tapa attire and synchronized group motion in an open-air island setting — Society Islands, French Polynesia.
